classification.difficultyReason: Track two ages through two time shifts, translate a fractional future ratio, clear its denominator and interpret fractional present ages within the prescribed simultaneous-equation strategy.

content.prompt:
Solve by introducing two pronumerals and forming two simultaneous equations, even though this problem may be done more easily using one pronumeral.

Four years ago Jie was twice Tan’s age. In four years’ time, Jie will be one and a quarter times Tan’s age. How old are Jie and Tan now?

answer.short: Jie is $9\frac{1}{3}$ years old and Tan is $6\frac{2}{3}$ years old.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ be Jie’s present age in years and $y$ be Tan’s present age in years.

Four years ago:
$$\begin{align*}x-4&=2(y-4)\\x-2y&=-4\qquad(1)\end{align*}$$

In four years’ time:
$$\begin{align*}x+4&=\frac{5}{4}(y+4)\\4x+16&=5y+20\\4x-5y&=4\qquad(2)\end{align*}$$

Multiply equation (1) by 4:
$$4x-8y=-16\qquad(3)$$

Subtract equation (3) from equation (2):
$$\begin{align*}(4x-5y)-(4x-8y)&=4-(-16)\\3y&=20\\y&=\frac{20}{3}\end{align*}$$

Substitute into equation (1):
$$\begin{align*}x-2\left(\frac{20}{3}\right)&=-4\\x&=-4+\frac{40}{3}\\x&=\frac{28}{3}\end{align*}$$

Jie is $9\frac{1}{3}$ years old and Tan is $6\frac{2}{3}$ years old.

Check: four years ago their ages were $\frac{16}{3}$ and $\frac{8}{3}$ years, so Jie was twice Tan’s age. In four years their ages will be $\frac{40}{3}$ and $\frac{32}{3}$ years, and $\frac{5}{4}\times\frac{32}{3}=\frac{40}{3}$.
